consent.title: Help improve Ankigen?
consent.description: May we send installation, activity and creation counts to PostHog? No documents or card content are shared. You can choose the categories below or change them later in Settings.
settings.analytics_details: Events include a random installation ID, event ID, time, app version, operating system family, counts and export format. There are no screen recordings or user profiles. Location enrichment is disabled; PostHog still receives your IP address as part of the connection. Usage is visible in the developer's private dashboard.
settings.analytics_withdrawal: You can turn this off and save at any time. Pending events are removed; a request already in progress may finish. Events already received remain under the dashboard's retention policy. The random ID stays on this device so enabling statistics again does not count as another installation. Offline events are kept for up to 7 days, with a maximum of 500 events.

help.anki_import: In Anki: File > Import, pick the .tsv file.
help.anki_media: If your cards use images, copy everything in the export's media/ folder into your Anki profile's collection.media folder, with Anki closed. The "Copy media into Anki" button does this for you.
help.intro: Ankigen turns a structured .docx course into an Anki deck, with you and Claude in the loop — it never invents cards on its own.
help.skill_intro: A skill is a folder holding a SKILL.md file: YAML frontmatter with a name and a description saying when to use it, then the instructions in Markdown. Claude loads it when the task matches, so you never paste the same instructions twice.
help.skill_location: Put it in your Claude skills folder, one folder per skill, then start a conversation and send it a chunk.
help.skill_template_help: Copy this into a SKILL.md file. It is a working starting point, not a rulebook — the HTML colour conventions are one person's habits, but the output format and the image/table placeholders are what Ankigen actually reads at export time.
help.step_chunks: Ankigen splits the document into chunks, one per section, and derives an Anki deck path from the heading hierarchy.
help.step_claude: Copy a chunk and send it to Claude, which has your card-writing skill loaded.
help.step_export: Export as TSV, or as ZIP when your cards use images.
help.step_paste: Paste Claude's tab-separated answer back, check the card preview, save, move to the next chunk.
help.step_upload: Import a .docx whose headings use real heading styles — that is what the splitting relies on.

help.timelines_caption: course → Claude → timeline → images, PDF, cards
help.timelines_intro: A timeline gathers the dates of a paragraph, a chapter or a whole course on a single drawing, with tracks, periods and eras. As with cards, Claude reads the course and Ankigen does the rest: Claude only returns the list of dates as JSON, and Ankigen draws the timeline itself, so labels never overlap.
help.timelines_step_scope: In the work view, the Timeline button offers three scopes: this paragraph, a chapter (one of the headings above the current paragraph) or the whole course. From the home page, New timeline starts from a pasted text or imports a JSON file.
help.timelines_step_prompt: Copy the prompt from the Prompt tab and send it to Claude. It carries the whole format, a worked example and the course text: nothing to set up.
help.timelines_step_paste: Paste Claude's JSON answer. If something is wrong, the app shows where and why, and gives you a correction prompt to send to the same conversation.
help.timelines_step_edit: Check the timeline and adjust it from the list on the left: date, label, track, importance. Apply, and the drawing updates at once.
help.timelines_step_export: Export it as PNG, JPEG, WebP, PDF (A4, A3 or fitted to the content), SVG or JSON, or turn it into Anki cards from the Cards tab.
help.timelines_long: Beyond about 25,000 characters, a single prompt makes the model skim. Ankigen then suggests one prompt per paragraph: the Sources list shows what is left to do, each answer is checked on its own, and the answers are merged into one timeline. Tracks with the same name are matched, and an event found in two paragraphs becomes one, keeping every quotation; you can separate a merge again from its details.
help.timelines_quotes_title: Is it really in the course?
help.timelines_quotes: Claude must copy, for each date, the sentence of the course it comes from. Ankigen looks for that quotation in the course: ≈ means it was found approximately, and ⚠ that it was not found at all, in which case the marker is ringed in the preview. In enriched mode, Claude may add a few context dates: they are marked ✦ “not in the course” and left out of the cards.
help.timelines_format_title: The JSON format and the Skill
help.timelines_format: A timeline is an ankigen.timeline/1 document: a title, up to 12 tracks, and eras, periods and events with their dates ("1971-08-15", "1971-08", "1971", "-44" for 44 BC). You can write or fix it by hand in the JSON tab. The JSON Schema lets a local model answer in the right format directly.
help.timelines_skill: The copied prompt already contains the whole format, so no Skill is needed. If you would rather keep the format in Claude, install this Skill and tick “I installed the Skill” in the Prompt tab: the copied prompt then shrinks to the course text.
help.timelines_skill_help: Save it as SKILL.md in an ankigen-timeline folder of your Claude skills. It is built from the same text as the prompt, so the two never drift apart.
help.timelines_cards: The Cards tab writes the cards itself, without Claude: “In which year…?”, “what happens on this date?”, period dates, putting events in order, before and after, and picture cards where an event is hidden on the timeline. Tick the types you want, turn off the cards you do not need, then export a TSV, a ZIP with the pictures, or copy the pictures straight into Anki. From the work view, the export can also include the cards of the course's timelines.
help.timelines_reimport: Re-importing after a change updates your notes instead of duplicating them: the front of each card only changes if its question does, and Anki matches notes on that first field. The deck is set once, when the cards are first generated, so it does not change if you switch the interface language.
help.timelines_limit_calendar: Dates use the Gregorian calendar as written: a date before 1582 is not converted from the Julian calendar. Geological time and other calendars are not supported. There is no year 0: 1 BC is followed by AD 1.
help.timelines_limit_sizes: A timeline holds at most 12 tracks, 20 eras, 200 periods and 400 events. When there are too many labels, some move to numbered notes under the timeline instead of overlapping.
help.timelines_limit_pdf: The PDF holds a 300 dpi picture of the timeline, not vector text. Exported images are capped at 60 megapixels; the export dialog warns you when a timeline has to be scaled down.
help.timelines_limit_fonts: Timelines use the Inter typeface, shipped with the app. Characters it does not have (Chinese, emoji…) are drawn as boxes, and the app warns you.
